retrieval_query: The Cowan Paradox: Why AI Agents Won’t Let You Do Less Work. They’ll Make You Do More.

trace.topic: The Cowan Paradox: Why AI Agents Won’t Let You Do Less Work. They’ll Make You Do More.
trace.goal: Explain the paradox that AI agents increase managerial and operational work.
expected_facts: The answer should explain that AI agents expand what teams can attempt, which often increases work.
It should argue that management, supervision, and orchestration become more important, not less.
It should connect the paradox to founder expectations about leverage.
rubric_must_haves: Names and explains the paradox clearly.
Connects the idea to day-to-day operating reality.
Includes a concrete implication for founders or managers.
trace.gold_reference: A strong answer should explain that AI agents create leverage, but leverage usually expands the amount of work teams attempt rather than shrinking the need for judgment and management. As a result, founders often find themselves supervising more workflows, more experiments, and more exceptions. The lesson is to expect amplified operations, not effortless simplification.

trace.answer:
The Cowan Paradox: Why AI Agents Won’t Let You Do Less Work. They’ll Make You Do More.
We’ve all heard the promise. We’re going to deploy some amazing AI agents and we’re going to get so much done. And it’s true—up to a point.
But here’s what nobody tells you:
Once you have the capability to do something well, you develop an insatiable desire to keep doing it
And when those capabilities become truly effortless? That’s where addiction kicks in.
I was talking with Rory O’Driscoll recently—he’s been investing in B2B for decades—and I asked him if he’d seen this dynamic play out elsewhere. His response crystallized exactly why I’m writing this today:
“There isn’t any parallel.”
No previous technology wave created this particular problem. Not email. Not mobile. Not SaaS itself. But here’s what I think happened: For the first time, we actually had something that worked so well on our behalf that we couldn’t help ourselves from using it constantly. The old paradigm made sense: you hire someone because they could do the work better than you could. Then you manage them because there’s a ceiling on how many hours anyone works per day. Your VP of Marketing might hit her goals perfectly—but she’s still only working 50-60 hour weeks. She takes vacation. She burns out eventually. There’s natural limits. Then came AI. Now your marketing agent doesn’t just work harder—it never stops working.
trace.raw_model_output:
The Cowan Paradox:
Why AI Agents Won’t Let You Do Less Work. They’ll Make You Do More
Most founders think AI will free them up to focus on high-level strategy while AI handles the grunt work. We’re wrong. What’s actually happening? And what does this mean for your business?
I’ve been using AI agents intensively since early 2024 – not just testing tools, but running real production workflows with hundreds of thousands of interactions per week across our portfolio companies. I’ve also interviewed over 100 SaaS leaders who have deployed similar systems. Here’s what we’ve learned, and it should change how you think about AI implementation entirely.
It’s Not About Efficiency
First, let me dispel a myth. No one bought Claude Code thinking “oh boy, now I can ship code faster.” That’s true. But here’s what nobody talks about: the bar went up. Now there’s no excuse for bad software. Every competitor ships fast. So if you don’t, you lose. Period. This isn’t about doing less work. It’s about doing more work better. The Real Problem Nobody Warned Us About
Here’s what I didn’t expect: AI agents make us all feel guilty when they outperform us. When Amelia (our AI agent) crushes a task in minutes that would take me hours, something breaks inside my brain. My mind starts racing with new ideas. I start wondering why I couldn’t have thought of those connections myself. I become obsessed with understanding exactly what she did differently. Then I’m hooked. I want to keep experimenting. To learn more patterns. To see where else these breakthroughs apply.

retrieval_hits.text: Because AI, used right, enables you to do more things at scale than were ever possible before.

"20 AI Agents aren't less work than the humans they replaced.

But it's just ... easier.  They don't quit, they don't stop, they don't need promotions or even career growth.

It's easier to work with well-trained AI Agents than ... mid-pack and below humans."  More below

This is why AI will soon take 50%+ of sales jobs

Not because we don’t need sales.  But because AI can do a better job than this.

2. The Always-On Pressure
Humans naturally create boundaries. We go home, we sleep, we disconnect. AI agents don’t. This creates an insidious pressure to match their pace.
I caught myself checking AI-generated reports at 11 PM because “the agents found something important.” This isn’t sustainable, and it’s not what AI was supposed to solve.
